headline: Review Tide Charts and State Park Access Requirements
reservation: Overnight stays in Cannon Beach require advance booking, especially for summer weekends and school holidays. Day-use entry for Ecola State Park is generally managed via on-site kiosks, but specific parking areas may reach capacity early. Changing coastal access policies and trail conditions require a direct check with Oregon State Parks before your visit.

days.title: Haystack Rock and Coastal Orientation
days.start: Suggested: 8 AM from Downtown Cannon Beach

stops.name: Haystack Rock
stops.detail: Walk the sandy shoreline to observe the intertidal area at a suitable low tide; look for Tufted Puffins nesting on the rock during spring and summer months.

stops.name: Hemlock Street
stops.detail: Explore the walkable village core to visit local art galleries and shops when coastal winds or rain make the beach less appealing.

days.driving: Allow 10 minutes locally; conditions vary by pedestrian traffic
days.note: Always check a local tide chart before walking toward headlands or intertidal zones.

days.title: Headlands and Forested Vistas
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from Cannon Beach North Entrance

stops.name: Ecola State Park
stops.detail: Drive to the main viewpoints for elevated perspectives of the coastline and offshore rocks, or walk the path toward Indian Beach if trail conditions permit.

stops.name: Terrible Tilly Viewpoint
stops.detail: Spot the historic Tillamook Rock Lighthouse offshore from the park’s northern overlooks.

days.driving: Allow 20–40 minutes; conditions vary by park road status
days.note: Park roads and trails are prone to seasonal erosion; verify status with official state park alerts.

days.title: Southern Sands and Scenic Coves
days.start: Suggested: 8:30 AM from Midtown Cannon Beach

stops.name: Hug Point State Recreation Site
stops.detail: Discover seasonal waterfalls and sea caves along the beach, ensuring you return before the incoming tide restricts access.

stops.name: Short Sand Beach
stops.detail: Follow the forested trail in Oswald West State Park down to a sheltered cove popular for surfing and birdwatching.

days.driving: Allow 30–50 minutes; conditions vary on US-101
days.note: Never turn your back on the ocean and watch for sneaker waves on exposed beaches.

intel.title: Downtown and Beach Access
intel.text: Public lots near Hemlock Street fill quickly during peak summer weekends; consider walking from your lodging if based in the village. Ecola State Park parking is limited and may be closed temporarily when capacity is reached.

intel.title: Coastal Connectivity
intel.text: Cellular service is generally reliable within the town of Cannon Beach but can become intermittent in the forested sections of Ecola and Oswald West State Parks. Download offline navigation for the drive south toward Manzanita.

intel.title: Service Hubs
intel.text: Fuel is available in Cannon Beach and the nearby gateway of Seaside to the north. Ensure your tank is sufficient before heading south into more remote stretches of the Tillamook Coast.

intel.title: Tide-Dependent Planning
intel.text: Intertidal exploration at Haystack Rock is best within an hour of low tide; verify daily charts as times shift significantly. Morning fog is common in summer and may obscure viewpoints until midday.

intel.title: Beach Stability
intel.text: Beach access points range from paved ramps to sandy paths; soft sand can be challenging for those with mobility aids. Check official updates for seasonal stairway removals or storm-related trail closures.

plan.arrival: Upon landing at PDX, collect your rental car and head west via US-26. Stop in Seaside for major grocery needs before checking into your Cannon Beach lodging.
plan.vehicle: A standard passenger car is sufficient for paved coastal roads; check rental agreements for any restrictions on unpaved park access points.
plan.goldenHour: Ecola Point offers a classic sunset view of Haystack Rock, though coastal fog may impact visibility seasonally.
